test_title: PYST 43: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 23 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: According to the Ministry of Finance, States’ SGST revenue, including compensation released to States, in the post-GST period of 2017-18 to 2022-23 has achieved a tax buoyancy of _______.
solution:
The Correct answer is __**more than 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the context of taxation, **tax buoyancy** measures the responsiveness of tax revenue growth to the growth of Gross Domestic Product (**GDP**).
 
• A tax buoyancy of **more than 1** indicates that tax revenue grows faster than the GDP, showcasing an efficient tax system.
 
• As per the **Ministry of Finance**, the **SGST (State Goods and Services Tax)** revenue, including compensation to states, has consistently demonstrated a buoyancy above 1 in the post-GST period from **2017-18 to 2022-23**.
 
• This reflects the success of the **GST implementation** in ensuring sustainable revenue growth for state governments while streamlining the taxation system.
 
• The introduction of GST replaced a complex tax structure with a unified system, enhancing compliance and improving revenue collection efficiency.
 
• The government has also provided **compensation** to states for any revenue shortfall due to the transition to GST, ensuring financial stability for states.
 
• This buoyancy signifies that GST has been instrumental in improving the tax-to-GDP ratio, contributing to fiscal consolidation goals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Zero**__

 __
 
• A tax buoyancy of **zero** implies no growth in tax revenue despite GDP growth, indicating inefficiency in the tax system.
 
• This scenario is unlikely for GST, as the tax reform has been designed to improve compliance and revenue collection.
 
 
 
• **Less than 1**__
 __
 
• A tax buoyancy of **less than 1** would mean that tax revenue grows at a slower rate than GDP, which is not reflective of the GST revenue trends observed in India.
 
• GST implementation has significantly improved tax collection efficiency, ensuring buoyancy above 1.
 
 
 
• **Greater than 10**__
 
 
• A tax buoyancy of **greater than 10** is an extreme and unrealistic figure, as it would imply an exceptionally high growth in tax revenue compared to GDP growth.
 
• Such a scenario is unlikely and not observed in the context of India's GST revenue.
